title: Parallel tool calls all sent with constant index=0; only ids distinguish calls
source: litellm#21331 (2026-02, Responses-API bridge hardcodes index=0) + ollama#15457 (2026-04, OpenAI-compatible endpoint always index 0); same class as Gemini C14

messages.content: What's the weather in Paris and the current UTC time?

anomalies.note: all tool_call deltas carry constant `index`=0 across two distinct calls (OpenAI requires index to identify the call being extended)
reconstruction only possible by keying on `id`; ids are present on every delta in this capture, which is itself a deviation (OpenAI sends id on the first delta only)

expected.note: Expected output has two separate, fully-assembled calls. Index-keyed accumulation merges or re-initializes them (both failure modes observed in source cases). Verdict is recoverable only because ids are consistent across deltas here; a variant where fragments lack ids AND index is constant must be reported as unrecoverable rather than silently merged.

failureModeIfBuggy: Index-keyed consumer merges both calls into one malformed tool call with concatenated arguments (`{"city":"Paris"}{"tz":"UTC"}`), or re-initializes the call on every id-bearing chunk, losing accumulated arguments.
mutationHooks: Remove ids from the two argument-fragment deltas — expected verdict must flip to unrecoverable (attribution ambiguous), proving the fixture encodes the recoverability condition, not just the happy path.
Change second call's index to 1 — anomalies must become empty, proving the anomaly fires on constant-index specifically.
specBasis: OpenAI Chat Completions streaming: `index` distinguishes parallel tool calls; fragments for different calls must not share an index.

Source case #21331 documents consumer-side merge under index=0 and the reporter's virtual-index workaround ('tool call IDs are unique and consistent across deltas, even when the streaming index is wrong').
notes: Covers the defect class independently observed in three ecosystems (see candidates list §1): Gemini compat endpoint (f2), LiteLLM Responses bridge (#21331), Ollama /v1 (#15457). Ollama #7881 documents the fully-missing-index variant — same recoverability logic as f2.
